title: Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription validity and expired-prescription continuation
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.04(12) a prescription for a Schedule VI medication is valid for ONE YEAR from the date of issue and a licensee may not refill a Schedule VI prescription after one year. If a Schedule VI prescription expires or has no remaining refills and the pharmacist is unable to obtain prescriber authorization in a timely manner, the pharmacist in his or her professional judgment may dispense a quantity NOT TO EXCEED 14 DAYS or the smallest available unit-of-use packaging. Under 247 CMR 9.04(15) the requirements of 247 CMR 9.04(12) do not apply to institutional sterile compounding pharmacies.
exam_relevance: Tests the Schedule VI validity clock and the narrow professional-judgment continuation supply, and whether the candidate keeps them separate from the Schedule VI transfer limit.

authority.name: Massachusetts requirements for dispensing and refilling prescriptions

numeric_facts.conditions: A licensee may not refill a Schedule VI prescription after one year

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum continuation supply when a Schedule VI prescription has lapsed
numeric_facts.conditions: Or the smallest available unit-of-use packaging, in the pharmacist's professional judgment, where prescriber authorization cannot be obtained in a timely manner

exceptions: 247 CMR 9.04(15) excludes institutional sterile compounding pharmacies from 247 CMR 9.04(12).
The continuation supply is a professional-judgment allowance conditioned on inability to obtain timely prescriber authorization; it is not an automatic refill.
common_confusions: Treating the 247 CMR 9.14(4)(c) one-year transfer bar as the only one-year Schedule VI rule and concluding that no general validity limit exists.
Reading the continuation allowance as authorising an ordinary refill after the one-year validity period.
Applying 247 CMR 9.04(12) to an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy.
verification_notes: 247 CMR 9.04(12) and 247 CMR 9.04(15) read verbatim in the current official Board publication dated 12/6/24 on 2026-09-04 during Study Guide REPAIR-V3, remediating the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V2 finding that no canonical rule carried the Schedule VI validity clock.
